theory.intro: When you know the area but not one side length, substitute what you do know into the area formula and solve the equation using inverse operations.
facts: Use $A=lw$ for a rectangle, $A=bh$ for a parallelogram and $A=\frac{bh}{2}$ for a triangle.
The height in $A=bh$ and $A=\frac{bh}{2}$ is the **perpendicular** height, not a slanted side.
Whatever you do to one side of the equation, do to the other so it stays balanced.
For a triangle, **multiply both sides by $2$ first**, then divide by the known length.
The answer is a length, so write it in a unit such as cm or m, not a squared unit.
steps: Write the formula for the shape.
Solve for the unknown using inverse operations.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) A rectangle has area $39.6\text{ m}^2$ and length $6\text{ m}$. Find its width.
(b) A parallelogram has area $84\text{ cm}^2$ and base $12\text{ cm}$. Find its perpendicular height.
A triangle has area $55\text{ cm}^2$ and perpendicular height $10\text{ cm}$ to the base. A slanted side is $13\text{ cm}$. Find the base length.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use the $10\text{ cm}$ perpendicular height; the slanted side is not needed.
$A=\frac{bh}{2}$
$55=\frac{10b}{2}$
$110=10b$
$b=11\text{ cm}$.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) A parallelogram has a base of $15\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $8\text{ cm}$. Another side is $10\text{ cm}$. Find the perpendicular height to that side.
(b) A triangle has base $21\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $8\text{ cm}$. A second perpendicular height of $12\text{ cm}$ is drawn to another side. Find the length of that side.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $A=bh$
$A=15\times8=120\text{ cm}^2$
$120=10h$
$h=12\text{ cm}$.
(b) $A=\frac{bh}{2}$
$A=\frac{21\times8}{2}=84\text{ cm}^2$
$84=\frac{12b}{2}$
$168=12b$
$b=14\text{ cm}$.
Each new base uses its own perpendicular height, while the area stays the same.

workedExamples.question_text: A rectangle is $10\text{ cm}$ by $6\text{ cm}$. A triangle has half its area and base $12\text{ cm}$. Find the triangle’s perpendicular height.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Rectangle area $=10\times6=60\text{ cm}^2$.
Triangle area $=60\div2=30\text{ cm}^2$.
$A=\frac{bh}{2}$
$30=\frac{12h}{2}$
$60=12h$
$h=5\text{ cm}$.

workedExamples.question_text: A smaller rectangle of area $21\text{ cm}^2$ and height $3\text{ cm}$ sits on the left of a larger rectangle. The larger rectangle extends $8\text{ cm}$ beyond it to the right and has area $150\text{ cm}^2$. Find the larger rectangle’s height.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Smaller rectangle: $A=lw$
$21=3w$
$w=7\text{ cm}$.
Larger rectangle width $=7+8=15\text{ cm}$.
$150=15h$
$h=10\text{ cm}$.

workedExamples.question_text: A parallelogram is divided into two smaller parallelograms with the same perpendicular height. The right part has base $15\text{ cm}$ and area $75\text{ cm}^2$. The left part has area $45\text{ cm}^2$. Find its base length.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Right part: $A=bh$
$75=15h$
$h=5\text{ cm}$.
Left part: $45=5b$
$b=9\text{ cm}$.
